engine_api.description: EL-CL communication via Engine API is authenticated using JWT and considered semi-trusted
engine_api.rationale: Co-located EL and CL clients communicate via authenticated Engine API (JWT). The Engine API is considered a trusted boundary, but data returned by EL may not be fully verified by CL in all cases (e.g., blob data from engine_getBlobsV2 is used without KZG verification). If the EL is compromised or buggy, corrupted data may be propagated to the network.
security_implications: Engine API is authenticated via JWT
Some data from EL may be used without full verification by CL
Compromised EL can affect CL behavior
engine_api.note: Vulnerabilities in Engine API implementation are in-scope, but attacks requiring a compromised local EL may be considered conditional or lower severity

local_validator.description: Local validator configuration is under operator control and considered semi-trusted
local_validator.rationale: Local validator configuration is under operator control. Misconfigured or manipulated validator settings could cause incorrect node behavior.
local_validator.note: Configuration issues requiring operator error are typically out-of-scope

p2p_peers.description: P2P network peers are unauthenticated and considered untrusted
p2p_peers.rationale: P2P network peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join the network and send arbitrary protocol messages. All P2P input must be fully validated.
p2p_peers.note: Vulnerabilities exploitable via P2P network are high priority for bug bounty

Critical.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Exploit an EIP/specification or client bug to easily create an infinite amount of ETH which is finalized by the network
Take down the entire network by sending a single malicious on-chain transaction that ends up crashing all clients
Critical.impact: Entire network (>50% validators or all clients)
Critical.attack_vector: Single malicious on-chain transaction or network packet

High.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 33% of the network
Bring down more than 33% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
High.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Medium.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting more than 5% of the network
Bring down more than 5% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Medium.impact: More than 5% of the network (or >1% of validators for slashing)
Medium.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Low.criteria: Vulnerabilities that allow an attacker to:
examples: Trivially cause network splits affecting at least 0.01% of the network
Bring down more than 0.01% of the network by sending a single network packet or an on-chain transaction
Low.attack_vector: Single network packet or on-chain transaction

Informational.criteria: Observations or recommendations regarding code quality, maintainability, or system architecture that do not present a direct security risk
Informational.validity_requirement: Only applicable if the team decides to implement a change based on the report
notes: Informational issues are valid if they don't lead to a sufficient impact to count as Low or higher and are valuable enough for the client that they decided to implement the change in the code
Issues related to parts under the 'Out of scope' section will not be considered valid
Informational issues won't have duplicates, and only the first one is valid
They also don't qualify for the 1st and 2nd week multipliers, as they apply only to issues in the main pot

el_vectors.threat: Submit malformed transactions, resource exhaustion via high-gas or oversized inputs
Eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks/transactions, propagate blocks with invalid gas limits

cl_vectors.threat: Propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, withhold data columns in PeerDAS
Return invalid column data, refuse to serve custody columns, send malformed KZG proofs

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via DAS Column Sampling
trusted_external_entities.rationale: P2P peers are unauthenticated. Any node can join and serve invalid column data or withhold columns. All received columns must be verified via KZG proofs.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Column Reconstruction Requests
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers providing missing columns for data reconstruction are unauthenticated. Column data must be KZG-verified before use in erasure code reconstruction.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P blob transaction gossip (with cell proofs)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blob transactions received via gossip are from untrusted sources. Blob count, quantity matching, cell proof count, KZG hash, and cell proof batch verification must all be performed.

trusted_external_entities.name: Blob Transaction Submitter via Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transactions entering the mempool via gossip are from untrusted peers. Full validation of wrapper format, cell proofs, and KZG commitments required.

trusted_external_entities.name: On-chain Caller via MODEXP Precompile
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: MODEXP precompile call (address 0x05) within EVM execution
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any contract or EOA can call the MODEXP precompile with arbitrary input. Input length bounds (1024 bytes) must be enforced before computation. Untrusted on-chain input.

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender (Gas Limit)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Transaction submission (RPC or P2P) with gasLimit field
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Transaction senders can set arbitrary gasLimit values. The 16,777,216 cap must be enforced at both mempool acceptance and block validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Block Broadcast
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Blocks received from peers may contain transactions exceeding the gas cap. Block-level validation must check each transaction's gasLimit against the 16,777,216 cap.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: P2P data column sampling response handler
boundary_edges.security_assumption: All received column samples MUST be verified via KZG proof batch verification before being accepted. Invalid proofs must result in column rejection and potential peer scoring penalty.
Columns received for reconstruction MUST be KZG-verified. Insufficient columns must not trigger unsafe reconstruction. Timeout handling must prevent indefinite waiting.

Full validation required: blob count <= 6, quantity matching (hashes/blobs/commitments), cell proof count = CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB * blob_count, KZG commitment-to-hash verification, and batch cell proof verification.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Transaction pool ingestion (blob transaction wrapper validation)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Wrapper format validation, cell proof verification, and KZG commitment checks must all pass before mempool acceptance.

Input length parameters (BASE, EXPONENT, MODULUS) MUST each be checked against the 1024-byte upper bound BEFORE any computation. Violations must consume all gas and return error. All client implementations must enforce this identically to avoid consensus splits.
Transaction gasLimit MUST be checked against the 16,777,216 (2^24) cap at mempool ingestion. Transactions exceeding the cap must be rejected.
Each transaction within a received block MUST have its gasLimit checked against the 16,777,216 cap. Blocks containing any transaction exceeding the cap must be rejected entirely.
